annotation_description: Attacking with Llanowar Elves into an opponent with Gran-Gran (1/2) on the battlefield risks losing the mana dork to a block for no real benefit. Even though Gran-Gran is tapped now, the attack only deals 1 damage. More importantly, Llanowar Elves is a mana producer that enables casting Ouroboroid on turn 4 (which needs GG + 2 more mana). Trading or losing the Elves for 1 damage is poor value when the Elves are critical for ramping into the 4-drop.

Choosing Forest for Multiversal Passage is suboptimal. The player already has Botanical Sanctum (G/U), Breeding Pool (G/U Forest Island), and Llanowar Elves (G). They have abundant green mana sources. Looking at their hand, the Mockingbird costs {X}{U} and they might need blue mana. More importantly, their deck likely runs blue cards alongside green. Choosing Island would have provided color diversity since they're already heavy on green sources. With Breeding Pool already being a Forest, choosing Island for the Passage would give better mana flexibility. That said, the Ouroboroid costs {2}{G}{G} which needs double green, and with Gene Pollinator providing any color, the difference is relatively small.

Should play Mountain from hand before casting spells. Playing the land first gives more mana flexibility and is standard correct sequencing. Additionally, the critical priority this turn should be removing Ouroboroid with Combustion Technique before it snowballs further - while both can be cast this turn, leading with removal of the must-answer threat is safer.

Boomerang Basics on Ouroboroid is a reasonable tempo play to deal with a threatening creature that puts +1/+1 counters on all of DSV3's creatures at the beginning of combat. However, Combustion Technique with 4 Lesson cards in graveyard (after casting Boomerang Basics) would deal 2+4=6 damage, but Ouroboroid is only a 1/3 base (though it could have counters from its own trigger). The question is whether bouncing Ouroboroid is better than killing it with Combustion Technique. After Boomerang Basics resolves and goes to the graveyard, there would be 5 Lessons in the graveyard, making Combustion Technique deal 7 damage. However, the sequencing matters: casting Boomerang Basics first (which is a Lesson) puts it in the graveyard, powering up Combustion Technique for later. But bouncing Ouroboroid means the opponent can just replay it. Combustion Technique would permanently remove it (exile it, even). The better line might have been to cast Combustion Technique targeting Ouroboroid directly - with 4 Lessons in graveyard (Willowrush Verge x2 aren't Lessons, but Stormchaser's Talent isn't a Lesson either - let me recheck the graveyard: Willowrush Verge, Willowrush Verge, Stormchaser's Talent, Abandon Attachments). Only Abandon Attachments is a Lesson in the graveyard, so Combustion Technique would deal 2+1=3 damage. Ouroboroid is 1/3 base but at beginning of combat gets +1/+1 counters equal to its power, so it could be bigger. Actually wait - it's currently on the battlefield as listed without any notation of counters, so it might be a 1/3 still (or could have gotten counters from previous combat). If it's a 1/3, 3 damage kills it. But if Boomerang Basics is cast first (it's a Lesson), then Combustion Technique deals 2+2=4. Either way, bouncing is only temporary removal while Combustion Technique would exile it permanently. Using Boomerang Basics here wastes the permanent removal opportunity since the opponent will just replay Ouroboroid next turn.

Casting a second Gran-Gran while already controlling one on the battlefield results in one being sacrificed to the legend rule, wasting a card for zero benefit. The existing Gran-Gran is untapped and functional - replacing it with an identical copy accomplishes nothing.

Casting a second Gran-Gran when one is already on the battlefield triggers the legend rule, requiring one to be sacrificed immediately. This wastes a card for just a single loot trigger (draw 1, discard 1), which is card-neutral at best. Meanwhile, the player has Combustion Technique available which could kill the opponent's Ouroboroid (a serious threat that puts +1/+1 counters on all creatures at the beginning of combat), and Accumulate Wisdom which draws cards without costing a card. Artist's Talent is also a strong option for ongoing value. The Ouroboroid is particularly dangerous as it will keep growing DSV3 Analyst's board each turn.

Passed on casting any spells in precombat main when Ouroboroid (1/3) is on the opponent's board, growing exponentially each combat. Combustion Technique deals 4 damage (2 + 2 Lessons in graveyard), which kills the 1/3 Ouroboroid. If left alive, Ouroboroid will grow itself and all of DSV3's creatures by +1/+1 each combat, quickly becoming unmanageable. Additionally, Artist's Talent could have been deployed for ongoing value.

Gem25P Trash chose not to attack with Gran-Gran and Otter tokens. Gran-Gran has a valuable loot trigger (draw then discard) whenever it becomes tapped, which attacking provides for free. The opponent has an Ouroboroid (1/3 that grows each combat) and some small creatures, but Gran-Gran is a 1/2 that can attack into no meaningful blockers that would want to trade down for it - the opponent's untapped creatures are Llanowar Elves (1/1) and Gene Pollinators (1/2), none of which profitably block Gran-Gran. Additionally, with 3 Lesson cards in the graveyard, Gran-Gran's cost reduction is active, making the loot even more valuable for finding and casting cheap spells. The Otter token(s) with prowess could also chip in damage. Not attacking means missing free card selection from Gran-Gran's loot trigger and free damage pressure.

Ouroboroid is an exponentially growing threat that puts +1/+1 counters equal to its power on ALL of DSV3's creatures each combat. It's currently a 1/3 and Combustion Technique can deal 4 damage (2 + 2 Lessons in graveyard), easily killing it. Left alive, it will snowball out of control - next turn it becomes a 2/4, then 4/6, while also buffing Llanowar Elves and Gene Pollinators. Gem25P has the mana available to cast Combustion Technique right now.

Earthbending a Breeding Pool (dual land producing G/U) instead of Multiversal Passage (which only produces G). If the land-creature dies, losing a dual land is worse than losing a mono-color land. Multiversal Passage is the least flexible mana source.

Combustion Technique (dealing ~4 damage) was used on Gene Pollinator, a mana dork, instead of a higher-value target. Ouroboroid is the most dangerous card on the opponent's board as it exponentially grows the entire board each combat. If Ouroboroid had grown beyond 4 toughness, Llanowar Elves (which has a +1/+1 counter and is growing each turn from Ouroboroid) or the incoming Badgermole Cub would still be better targets than a Gene Pollinator.

annotation_description: Spider-Sense targeted itself instead of a meaningful spell on the stack. The stack contained Combustion Technique (which would likely kill Ouroboroid, the deck's key threat) and Accumulate Wisdom, both valid and important targets. Wasting the counter spell on itself means Combustion Technique resolves and likely removes Ouroboroid, while also losing the Spider-Sense for nothing.

annotation_description: Ouroboroid is an exponentially scaling threat that grows itself and all of DSV3's creatures every combat. With only Firebending Lesson (2 damage) as removal in hand, Gem25P needs to dig for real answers. A 1/1 Otter token does very little against increasingly large creatures.

Gem25P Trash incorrectly believed they had no red mana available, but had Mountain, two Spirebluff Canals, and Steam Vents all untapped (5 lands total). With Gran-Gran's cost reduction active (4 Lessons in graveyard), Artist's Talent costs only {R}. They could have cast Artist's Talent and Firebending Lesson, and potentially leveled up Stormchaser's Talent, all in the same turn. Instead they passed doing nothing against a rapidly growing Ouroboroid board.

Gem25P Trash has 4 potential attackers (Gran-Gran + 3 Otter tokens) against only one untapped blocker (Ouroboroid). Attacking with all would guarantee at least 3 creatures get through unblocked for 3+ damage, and Gran-Gran's tap trigger provides a free draw+discard for card quality. Even attacking Gran-Gran alone gives free card filtering with minimal risk. The opponent is at 12 life so chip damage matters.

Player incorrectly believed they had no red mana sources when they had Mountain, Steam Vents, and two Spirebluff Canals available. This caused them to pass the turn doing nothing instead of deploying Artist's Talent (a strong card advantage engine for 1R) and/or casting Firebending Lesson, or leveling up Stormchaser's Talent to get back a spell from graveyard. Missing deploying Artist's Talent is particularly costly as it provides ongoing card filtering with every noncreature spell cast.
